explanation: Support groups and counseling help families cope with the emotional and physical challenges of the grieving process. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T14#GNS324_U5_T14_h8)

question: As a nurse, what major emotional or psychological challenge should you anticipate for a patient facing a radical hysterectomy?

options.A: Complete loss of long-term memory function
options.B: Sudden denial of the physical diagnosis by family members
options.C: Intense fear of hospital food and environmental sounds
options.D: Body image disturbance and grief over lost fertility

explanation: Spot on. Losing reproductive organs can trigger profound emotional grief regarding womanhood, body image, and the ability to have children. Compassionate nursing support is everything here.

question: Why does milk make it so easy for bacteria to grow quickly?

options.A: It is usually stored in open containers in the market
options.B: It undergoes heavy chemical processing before packaging
options.C: It contains a high concentration of essential nutrients
options.D: It is naturally warm and has a very low pH level

explanation: Spot on! Milk is packed with proteins, fats, and sugars, which makes it a rich food source for microorganisms to feed and multiply on.

question: A cancer patient on a Step Two weak opioid still has severe pain. What should you do next?

options.A: Continue the current dose because ladder steps cannot be skipped
options.B: Discontinue all pain medications until the pain resolves naturally
options.C: Encourage the patient to rely strictly on relaxation breathing
options.D: Advocate for moving up to Step Three with a strong opioid

explanation: The pain ladder is flexible! If a weaker step isn't cutting it, it's time to step up to stronger medications to keep the patient comfortable.

question: Why are routine screenings, like annual tuberculosis tests, so important for hospital staff?

options.A: They completely prevent bacteria from entering the hospital building
options.B: They catch potential occupational infections early before symptoms worsen
options.C: They replace the need for wearing masks during patient care
options.D: They test the patient population for chronic illnesses

explanation: Routine checks help catch any sneaky occupational exposures early on, meaning you can get treated quickly and stay healthy!

question: Why are polyvalent nurses a lifesaver during staff shortages?

options.A: They only work during night shifts
options.B: They do not require supervision from senior staff
options.C: They can be deployed easily to different hospital units
options.D: They demand lower salaries than specialized nurses

explanation: You got it! Because they have a mix of skills, hospitals can easily move them to busy or understaffed wards to keep patient care running smoothly.

question: What is a simple, practical way to store extra green vegetables when electricity is unreliable?

options.A: Sealing in airtight glass jars with heavy salt
options.B: Soaking them continuously in vinegar
options.C: Sun-drying or blanching
options.D: Deep-freezing for three years

explanation: Correct! Sun-drying and blanching are time-tested ways to keep your veggies from spoiling without needing a fridge.

question: As a nurse, what is the very first test you should expect or check when a patient comes in with delayed menses?

options.A: Serum pregnancy test
options.B: Hysterosalpingogram
options.C: Diagnostic laparoscopy
options.D: Endometrial biopsy

explanation: Always rule out pregnancy first! In any woman of childbearing age with a missed or late period, checking for pregnancy is the mandatory first step.

question: Why do we have formal research guidelines like the Belmont Report in healthcare?

options.A: To help hospitals make more money
options.B: To prevent exploitation and protect human participants from harm
options.C: To guarantee positive study results
options.D: To speed up drug approvals

explanation: Exactly! Past abuses taught us that research participants need strong, guaranteed protection for their safety and rights.

question: Why do we frequently place a pregnant woman in shock on her left side?

options.A: To make it easier to perform a cesarean section locally
options.B: To stop excessive postpartum bleeding instantly
options.C: To speed up the delivery of the placenta
options.D: To prevent the heavy uterus from pressing on major blood vessels

explanation: Brilliant! Lying on the left side takes the heavy weight off the inferior vena cava, helping blood flow smoothly back to the heart. Simple trick, life-saving result!

question: How can pregnant women hold onto extra water and sodium without their blood pressure shooting up?

options.A: Renal tubules stop working completely in the second trimester.
options.B: The heart pumps with a much weaker force.
options.C: Excess fluid is immediately stored in the amniotic sac.
options.D: Systemic vascular resistance decreases at the same time.

explanation: Blood vessels relax and widen during pregnancy, giving the extra fluid plenty of room so blood pressure stays nice and stable.

question: What delicate structure separates the right and left lateral ventricles from each other?

options.A: Septum pellucidum
options.B: Cerebral aqueduct
options.C: Corpus callosum
options.D: Choroid plexus

explanation: Well done! The septum pellucidum is a thin, thin wall that sits right down the middle, separating the two lateral ventricles.

question: How does a nurse's role change during disaster monitoring compared to routine bedside care?

options.A: The focus shifts toward population health and community-wide safety
options.B: Nurses stop caring for individual patients entirely
options.C: Administrative paperwork replaces all hands-on nursing duties
options.D: Clinical assessment skills are no longer needed in the field

explanation: While bedside care focuses on one patient at a time, disaster monitoring broadens the nurse's view to entire communities and resource tracking. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T2#GNS315_U5_T2_h1)

question: Why can frequent exposure to high scrotal heat, like hot baths or saunas, lower a man's fertility?

options.A: It interferes with normal sperm production and development
options.B: It destroys the prostate gland and seminal vesicles
options.C: It blocks the release of testosterone from the adrenal glands
options.D: It causes permanent scarring of the vas deferens tubes

explanation: Fantastic! Sperm need a cozy spot slightly cooler than normal body temperature to grow properly, so extra heat disrupts the whole process.

question: Which of the following is NOT a standard nursing duty under the Mother-Baby Package?

options.A: Educating mothers on exclusive breastfeeding practices
options.B: Conducting routine antenatal assessments and checkups
options.C: Administering childhood immunizations according to the schedule
options.D: Performing elective major surgeries in primary health clinics

explanation: Correct! Major surgeries belong in a surgical theater with a doctor, not at a basic primary health clinic.

question: What is the most important advice for a patient who forgets to take their daily anticoagulant dose?

options.A: Stop taking the medication for the rest of the week
options.B: Double the next two doses to make up for lost time
options.C: Follow the specific clinic guidelines for missed doses
options.D: Take a double dose immediately to catch up

explanation: Never let a patient guess! Doubling up can cause dangerous bleeding, so they should always check their clinic's missed-dose policy. You nailed it!

question: How does endocrine signaling mostly differ from the nervous system?

options.A: Endocrine organs use ducts to release chemicals.
options.B: Nervous responses use hormones instead of electricity.
options.C: Endocrine responses are slower and last longer.
options.D: Nervous signals target every cell in the body at once.

explanation: You got it! While nervous system signals flash by in a split second, endocrine signals travel through the blood and take their time to create lasting effects.

question: What does 'participatory governance' mean in primary health care?

options.A: Leaving all health decisions entirely to elected politicians
options.B: Allowing only doctors to vote on clinic budgets
options.C: Involving local community members in health planning and decisions
options.D: Handing over total hospital ownership to private investors

explanation: Spot on! Participatory governance means the community isn't just a receiver of care—they help shape the health services they get. Keep up the great work!

question: A school suddenly reports many students down with waterborne gastroenteritis. Which management duty failed here?

options.A: Provision of infrastructure and clean water
options.B: Budget allocation for sports equipment
options.C: Teacher salary negotiations
options.D: Curriculum integration for health education

explanation: Spot on. Waterborne illnesses are a clear warning sign that safe drinking water and proper sanitation need urgent attention.

question: How do peer support groups help teenagers living with a chronic condition like HIV?

options.A: They eliminate the side effects of antiretroviral medications.
options.B: They replace the need for professional nursing assessments entirely.
options.C: They reduce feelings of isolation and encourage treatment adherence.
options.D: They provide financial loans for higher education expenses.

explanation: Well done! Connecting with others facing the same journey helps teens share tips, stay on their meds, and realize they aren't alone.

question: What is a virtual health community?

options.A: An online space where people connect for health support
options.B: A physical clinic equipped with virtual reality headsets
options.C: A government database of all registered nurses in a country
options.D: An emergency ambulance fitted with satellite navigation

explanation: You got it! Think of online support groups, health forums, and social media pages where people share health tips.

question: A home nurse finds a family completely exhausted from caring for an aging relative with dementia. What should the nurse do?

options.A: Report the family to social authorities for failing to provide basic care
options.B: Tell the family they must immediately place the relative in a permanent hospital
options.C: Advise them to stop providing care and leave the patient alone during the day
options.D: Connect the family with community support services and respite care options

explanation: Caregiver burnout is so real! Linking exhausted families with professional relief and respite care helps everyone keep going safely.

question: Why should you separate normal general waste from hazardous medical waste right from the start?

options.A: It ensures all waste can be recycled together safely.
options.B: It eliminates the need for any protective gear during disposal.
options.C: It reduces the volume of expensive hazardous waste treatment.
options.D: It allows general waste to be incinerated at high temperatures.

explanation: Treating medical waste safely is very costly. Keeping ordinary rubbish separate stops us from spending extra money and wasting precious resources on treating harmless items!

question: Which part of the teenage brain is still maturing and plays a big role in impulse control and risk-taking?

options.A: Cerebellum
options.B: Occipital lobe
options.C: Prefrontal cortex
options.D: Medulla oblongata

explanation: Correct! The prefrontal cortex develops slowly into early adulthood, which explains why teenagers sometimes struggle with weighing long-term consequences.

question: What is a major bottleneck when trying to execute the Nigerian health budget?

options.A: Delayed release of approved funds by treasury authorities
options.B: Excessive availability of cash at the primary clinic level
options.C: Automatic approval of all health sector requests
options.D: Complete absence of legislative review

explanation: Even when a budget looks great on paper, getting the actual cash released to clinics often takes a frustratingly long time.

question: Why do we need clear, agreed-upon definitions when collecting data for quality improvement?

options.A: To ensure everyone interprets and measures terms in the exact same way
options.B: To make the research paper long enough for publication
options.C: To increase the financial budget allocated to the nursing unit
options.D: To prove that nurses are working faster than doctors

explanation: Clear definitions mean everyone is speaking the same language, so the data we collect across different shifts is reliable and true.

question: In what year was the VAPP Act passed into law in Nigeria to protect people against violence?
explanation: Spot on! The VAPP Act was enacted in May 2015 to give survivors a strong legal backing against domestic violence and abuse.

question: A community living in a very dry, semi-arid desert region is most likely to depend on what primary food source?

options.A: Tropical root vegetables
options.B: Deep-sea marine fish
options.C: Livestock and pastoral products
options.D: Paddy rice cultivation

explanation: When dry climates make traditional crop farming difficult, communities naturally rely on raising hardy animals that can survive the harsh weather.

question: What is the biggest risk when a country relies heavily on foreign donor funding for healthcare?

options.A: Patients will refuse to take modern medications
options.B: The government will collect too much tax revenue locally
options.C: Programs may collapse if donor priorities or foreign policies change
options.D: Hospitals will automatically stop accepting local currency

explanation: Foreign aid can be unpredictable. If donors suddenly change their minds or pack up and leave, local health programs can fall apart if there's no backup plan.

question: Which hormone do all standard pregnancy test kits look for in blood or urine?

options.A: Human chorionic gonadotropin
options.B: Luteinizing hormone
options.C: Human placental lactogen
options.D: Follicle-stimulating hormone

explanation: hCG (Human chorionic gonadotropin) is the famous pregnancy hormone released right after a fertilized egg implants. That's what turns the test strip positive!

question: What is the primary focus of a physiatrist in a rehabilitation setting?

options.A: Restoring overall function and managing physical medicine
options.B: Managing hospital finances and administrative admissions
options.C: Conducting psychological counseling for depressed patients
options.D: Performing emergency orthopedic surgeries in the operating room

explanation: A physiatrist is a medical doctor who specializes in helping patients regain lost physical abilities and managing non-surgical recovery. [learn more](GNS123_U6_T3#GNS123_U6_T3_h3)

question: When is an assisted vaginal delivery using forceps preferred over an emergency caesarean section?

options.A: When the cervix is fully dilated and the baby's head is low
options.B: When the mother refuses all forms of surgical operations
options.C: When the baby is still floating high above the pelvic brim
options.D: When there is a complete prolapse of the umbilical cord

explanation: Forceps or vacuum delivery is only safe and appropriate when the cervix is fully open and the baby's head has descended deep into the pelvis. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T003#GNS226_U4_T003_h6)

question: A mother asks why her toddler needs a mix of both animal and plant proteins. What's the best way to answer?

options.A: Mixing them ensures the child gets all the essential building blocks for growth
options.B: Animal proteins contain no essential amino acids on their own
options.C: Plant proteins are toxic to the kidneys of young children
options.D: Only animal proteins can provide energy for daily physical activities

explanation: Spot on. Combining different protein sources helps make sure the child gets every essential amino acid their growing body needs!

question: An older client with dementia relies totally on her son for baths and medication. Why is she at high risk for abuse?

options.A: She is exposed to many different community health workers daily
options.B: She has financial independence from her family
options.C: Her physical and cognitive dependence creates a severe power imbalance
options.D: Older adults are naturally immune to domestic coercion

explanation: Exactly. When a patient depends completely on just one person for basic daily needs, it opens the door wide to potential abuse.

question: What is the main difference between tertiary and secondary healthcare?

options.A: Tertiary care involves highly specialized sub-specialists and advanced technology
options.B: Tertiary care is located in every small rural village across the country
options.C: Secondary care requires medical students for operation, unlike tertiary care
options.D: Secondary care handles complex brain surgery while tertiary care handles basic immunization

explanation: When cases get super complex, they go to tertiary centers. They have advanced technology and sub-specialists that standard general hospitals don't usually have.

question: Why do major burn survivors need a massive amount of protein in their diet while recovering?

options.A: To offset massive protein catabolism and support wound healing
options.B: To maintain normal blood pressure by increasing plasma volume
options.C: To prevent the development of permanent metabolic acidosis
options.D: To suppress the inflammatory immune response completely

explanation: Major burns put the body into overdrive, burning through muscle and protein super fast. High protein intake feeds the repair process so new tissue can grow.

question: Which specific vitamin needs a special helper protein called 'intrinsic factor' from the stomach to be absorbed properly?

options.A: Folic acid
options.B: Vitamin B12
options.C: Vitamin K
options.D: Vitamin C

explanation: Intrinsic factor is like a VIP escort for Vitamin B12! It teams up in the stomach to protect the vitamin until they reach the lower part of the small intestine for absorption.

question: What happens to spermatids during the spermiogenesis phase?

options.A: They remodel their shape and develop a tail without dividing again
options.B: They combine with fluid from the prostate gland
options.C: They multiply rapidly through standard cell division
options.D: They travel out of the scrotum into the urinary bladder

explanation: Spermiogenesis is purely a structural remodeling phase where round cells transform into streamlined swimming sperm. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T7#GNS216_U2_T7_h4)

question: A nurse cares for a patient with a drug-resistant wound infection. Which principle guides safe nursing care?

options.A: Treating all patient blood and body fluids as infectious using standard precautions
options.B: Reusing medical equipment between patients if it looks visually clean
options.C: Stopping all hand hygiene once gloves are removed from the hands
options.D: Assuming infection control is only necessary if the patient shows a high fever

explanation: Standard precautions require treating all bodily fluids as potentially infectious to protect against both known and unknown pathogens. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T6#GNS313_U1_T6_h8)

question: What is a fixed cost in a health care facility?

options.A: An expense that increases every time a new patient is admitted
options.B: Wages paid to temporary agency nurses working extra shifts
options.C: An expense that does not change when patient volume changes
options.D: The price of consumable medical supplies like syringes

explanation: Fixed costs, like building rent, stay exactly the same whether the ward is completely full or nearly empty.

question: What is one of the best perks of using an electronic blood pressure machine over a manual one?

options.A: They are completely unaffected if the patient moves
options.B: They take very little training to use correctly
options.C: They give exact readings even during serious heart rhythm problems
options.D: They never need new batteries or servicing

explanation: Digital monitors do the heavy lifting for you! You don't need expert stethoscope listening skills to get a quick reading.

question: What is the main purpose of health education in schools?

options.A: To train students to become qualified medical doctors
options.B: To fill up empty timetable periods with lectures
options.C: To promote positive behavioral changes and healthy habits
options.D: To replace practical nursing clinical rotations

explanation: Health education aims to give students the knowledge and attitude needed to adopt healthy lifestyles. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T3#GNS225_U4_T3_h4)

question: What is the most effective way to prevent severe maternal distress during childbirth?

options.A: Providing continuous physical and emotional labor support
options.B: Isolating the mother to encourage quiet rest
options.C: Delaying pain relief until the second stage of labor
options.D: Restricting fluid intake throughout the entire first stage

explanation: Never underestimate the power of a caring nurse holding a hand and offering words of encouragement. Being present is the best medicine!

question: What three categories are evaluated using the Glasgow Coma Scale?

options.A: Heart rate, breathing rate, and blood pressure
options.B: Eye opening, verbal response, and motor response
options.C: Reflex speed, muscle tone, and pain tolerance
options.D: Cranial nerve integrity, balance, and coordination

explanation: The Glasgow Coma Scale measures these three specific behavioral responses to quantify a patient's level of consciousness. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T1#GNS222_U3_T1_h8)

question: What is the safest medication choice to control blood sugar in gestational diabetes?

options.A: Metformin
options.B: Insulin
options.C: Acarbose
options.D: Glyburide

explanation: Insulin is the top choice because it generally doesn't cross over the placenta to the baby, keeping blood sugar managed safely.

question: What is the go-to treatment for primary hyperparathyroidism caused by a single adenoma?

options.A: Surgical removal of the affected gland
options.B: Strict dietary restriction of all dairy products
options.C: Complete removal of the entire thyroid gland
options.D: Long-term high-dose oral calcitonin therapy

explanation: Taking out the troublesome adenoma through surgery (parathyroidectomy) is the quickest way to cure primary hyperparathyroidism.

question: What is the main job of 'moulding' during labour?

options.A: To increase the total volume of brain tissue
options.B: To permanently fuse the cranial sutures early
options.C: To prevent the baby from breathing amniotic fluid
options.D: To reduce the skull dimensions to fit the pelvis

explanation: Moulding is the baby's superpower for birth! The skull bones gently overlap so the head shapes itself to fit easily through the birth canal without harming the brain.

question: Where does a nursing manager's primary power to direct a ward come from?

options.A: Advanced clinical certifications and degrees
options.B: Personal popularity among the nursing staff
options.C: Official position within the organizational hierarchy
options.D: Length of service in the specific hospital

explanation: You've got this! Managerial authority comes right from the official office or role you hold in the hospital structure, not just from being popular or having extra degrees. Keep pushing!

question: Why is keeping the head of a ventilated patient's bed elevated at 30 to 45 degrees such an important nursing action?

options.A: Endotracheal tube cuff rupture
options.B: Diaphragmatic muscle atrophy
options.C: Ventilator-associated pneumonia
options.D: Barotrauma from high tidal volumes

explanation: Gravity is our friend here! Elevating the bed stops oral and stomach fluids from pooling above the tube cuff and trickling down into the lungs to cause pneumonia.

question: What is the best move when a nurse is giving diet advice to a patient with a tight budget?

options.A: Handing them a strict shopping list of expensive imported supplements
options.B: Focusing only on rare medical terms without explaining the food items
options.C: Telling them to completely stop eating all traditional carbohydrate staples
options.D: Suggesting affordable local food substitutions that fit the patient's budget

explanation: Brilliant! Good nursing care meets patients where they are financially, offering realistic, pocket-friendly local food options.

question: Why are advance directives so helpful in critical or end-of-life care?

options.A: They guarantee that the patient will recover fully
options.B: They guide medical treatment according to the patient's prior wishes
options.C: They eliminate all paperwork for the hospital staff
options.D: They give the doctor total control over all decisions

explanation: Advance directives let patients make their choices known ahead of time, taking the guesswork out of difficult situations.

question: Which part of an antibody molecule binds directly to a specific antigen?

options.A: Y-shaped stem
options.B: Complement tail
options.C: Constant region
options.D: Variable region

explanation: The tips of the Y-shaped antibody have a variable region that fits onto antigens like a lock and key.

question: Why do social factors like poverty play such a big role in NCDs?

options.A: They ensure that patients always adhere strictly to their medication regimen
options.B: They directly cause genetic mutations that trigger cancer within weeks
options.C: They limit access to healthy foods, safe exercise spaces, and proper healthcare
options.D: They completely eliminate the risk of developing infectious diseases

explanation: Exactly! When money is tight, it becomes much harder to afford nutritious food, find safe places to exercise, or visit the clinic early for check-ups.

question: How do broken elevators and inaccessible buildings directly affect a disabled person's mental health?

options.A: They automatically cure chronic depression by forcing daily exercise
options.B: They improve social bonds by encouraging neighbors to carry people
options.C: They have no impact on emotions, only on physical fitness
options.D: They lead to physical exclusion, which triggers deep loneliness and isolation

explanation: That's right. When buildings aren't accessible, individuals get trapped at home, cutting off their social life and leading to heavy isolation.

question: Which type of germ is the absolute hardest to kill with standard chemical disinfectants?

options.A: Vegetative bacteria
options.B: Enveloped respiratory viruses
options.C: Gram-positive cocci
options.D: Bacterial endospores

explanation: Endospores have built-in super coats that make them amazingly resistant to heat, drying, and harsh chemicals.

question: When is an emergency caesarean section a must instead of giving drugs to speed up labour?

options.A: When the cervix is four centimetres dilated
options.B: When the mother feels mild fatigue
options.C: When membranes rupture spontaneously
options.D: When cephalopelvic disproportion is present

explanation: If the pelvis is too small for the baby (CPD), giving drugs to force contractions would be very dangerous and could cause the uterus to rupture. Surgery is life-saving here!

question: Why must you confirm a bed is ready at the receiving hospital before you even launch the evacuation?

options.A: To ensure the transport vehicle has enough fuel for the trip
options.B: To let the pilot know which runway is clear for landing
options.C: To calculate the exact financial cost of the hospital stay
options.D: To prevent dangerous delays upon arrival at the destination

explanation: Arriving at a busy hospital with no bed ready wastes precious time and leaves your vulnerable patient stuck waiting inside the transport vehicle.

question: What are the two main synthetic hormones used in most hormonal birth control methods?

options.A: Thyroxine and calcitonin
options.B: Estrogen and progestin
options.C: Cortisol and aldosterone
options.D: Insulin and glucagon

explanation: Great start! Hormonal contraceptives work by mimicking natural female hormones using synthetic forms of estrogen and progestin to keep the cycle regulated and prevent pregnancy.

question: Which of the following is an example of a quantitative indicator used to evaluate community mobilisation?

options.A: Increased immunization coverage rates
options.B: Feelings of joy among committee members
options.C: Stories told by elders about past epidemics
options.D: The tone of voice used during town hall meetings

explanation: Quantitative indicators involve measurable numbers and statistics, such as vaccination percentages or clinic attendance counts. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T4#GNS124_U4_T4_h7)

question: What does the therapeutic use of a medication describe?

options.A: The chemical formula written on the manufacturing bottle
options.B: The exact physical size and color of the pill
options.C: The specific disease or condition the drug is used to treat
options.D: The country where the medication was originally made

explanation: Therapeutic use refers to the clinical condition or illness that the drug is meant to manage or cure. [learn more](GNS125_U2_T1#GNS125_U2_T1_h2)

question: Why is wearing a face shield so important when you are about to drain an abscess?

options.A: To keep the sterile instrument tray completely dry
options.B: To reduce the patient's anxiety during local numbing
options.C: To prevent accidental splashes of infected pus and blood
options.D: To filter out room dust from entering the open cavity

explanation: Pus inside an abscess is often under pressure. When the incision is made, it can squirt unexpectedly—protecting your eyes and face is a must!

question: What kind of authority does a nurse have when others listen to them purely because of their special clinical skills and advanced training?

options.A: Traditional authority
options.B: Charismatic authority
options.C: Formal authority
options.D: Expert authority

explanation: Brilliant! When respect and obedience come from your deep knowledge and specialized skills, that's your 'expert authority' shining through.

question: In a brain-injured patient, what does a sudden change in pupil size or reactivity usually tell you?

options.A: Increased intracranial pressure or brainstem compression
options.B: A minor infection of the outer ear canal
options.C: An allergic reaction to routine hospital bedding
options.D: Normal recovery from the primary neurological injury

explanation: The nerves that control your pupils run right past vital brain structures, making them very sensitive early warning signs of dangerous brain pressure.

question: What does the 'impersonal' aspect of the Hot Stove Rule mean?

options.A: Discipline targets the behavior, not the person
options.B: Rules apply only to new nursing staff members
options.C: Managers should never speak to the nurse directly
options.D: Penalties are handed out by a computer program

explanation: Fair discipline focuses purely on what the worker did wrong rather than attacking who they are. [learn more](GST321_U1_T22#GST321_U1_T22_h3)

question: Why is diet therapy such an important part of your daily nursing duties?

options.A: Nurses must personally cook all meals served in the hospital ward
options.B: Nurses are responsible for monitoring patient tolerance and supporting the prescribed nutrition plan
options.C: Dietary plans replace the need for physical assessments
options.D: Doctors never check what patients are eating

explanation: Since you spend the most time with patients, you are in the best position to see if they are enjoying their food and how well their body is handling it!

question: Why is a little bit of variation totally normal in the hospital?

options.A: Because hospital policies change during every shift handover
options.B: Because nurses rarely follow established clinical guidelines
options.C: Because individual patients respond differently to treatments
options.D: Because medical equipment is designed to malfunction regularly

explanation: Spot on! Every patient has a unique body and medical history, meaning their healing journey will naturally have slight differences.

question: A nurse tests a new pain medication and measures the patient's reported pain score. What represents the independent variable?

options.A: The reported pain score
options.B: The new pain medication
options.C: The patient's age
options.D: The hospital noise level

explanation: The medication is what the researcher changes or gives to the patient, making it the independent variable (the cause). [learn more](GNS224_U1_T7#GNS224_U1_T7_h4)

question: A stroke patient is struggling with swallowing food safely and speaking clearly. Who should the nurse call for help?

options.A: Speech-language pathologist
options.B: Social worker
options.C: Prosthetist
options.D: Physiotherapist

explanation: Speech therapists are experts at helping patients overcome both communication hurdles and swallowing issues (dysphagia).

question: At what point in their journey can a cancer patient start receiving palliative care?

options.A: When the patient's life expectancy drops below two weeks
options.B: Once the patient is admitted to a dedicated hospice facility
options.C: At the time of diagnosis, alongside active curative treatments
options.D: Only after all forms of chemotherapy and radiation have failed

explanation: Brilliant! Palliative care isn't just for end-of-life; it can—and should—start right from diagnosis to help manage symptoms while active treatment happens.

question: What is a key daily responsibility of the nurse regarding barrier nursing?

options.A: Writing new infectious disease policies
options.B: Testing hospital water supplies daily
options.C: Ordering all hospital cleaning supplies
options.D: Ensuring proper compliance with infection control rules

explanation: Nurses must actively monitor and maintain infection control standards during every shift to protect patients and staff. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T16#GNS122_U2_T16_h8)

question: Which physical finding should immediately make a nurse suspect physical abuse?

options.A: Bruises in various stages of healing across the arms and torso
options.B: Mild redness on pressure points caused by standard wheelchair use
options.C: Symmetrical skin discoloration commonly found on the lower shins
options.D: Fading surgical scars from an operation performed years ago

explanation: Injuries healing at different times point to repeated trauma rather than a single accidental fall. Great clinical spotting!

question: Which common bacterial infection is famous for causing silent damage that can lead to infertility if ignored?

options.A: Candidiasis
options.B: Chlamydia
options.C: Pubic lice
options.D: Bacterial vaginosis

explanation: Chlamydia is often called a 'silent' infection because it sneaks in without symptoms while quietly harming the fallopian tubes.

question: In Nigeria's routine immunization schedule, which vaccines are given right at birth?

options.A: Measles 1, Yellow Fever, and Meningitis
options.B: Pentavalent 1, PCV 1, and Rotavirus 1
options.C: BCG, OPV 0, and Hepatitis B birth dose
options.D: Inactivated Polio Vaccine and Tetanus toxoid

explanation: Always remember the birth trio: BCG, oral polio zero (OPV 0), and the Hepatitis B birth dose are given before the baby leaves the maternity ward!

question: What visual acuity score in the better eye (even with glasses) is generally used to define legal blindness?

options.A: 20/70 or worse
options.B: 20/40 or worse
options.C: 20/100 or worse
options.D: 20/200 or worse

explanation: You've got this! Legal blindness is officially classified as having a corrected visual acuity of 20/200 or lower in the better eye.

question: Which of the following is a modifiable risk factor for hypertension?

options.A: Family genetic history
options.B: Chronological aging
options.C: Biological sex
options.D: High dietary salt intake

explanation: Modifiable risk factors are lifestyle habits or conditions that a person can change, such as reducing salt intake, unlike age or genetics. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T14#GNS214_U1_T14_h2)

question: What important safety advice should a nurse give a patient about stopping anticholinergic drugs?

options.A: Stop taking them right away if your mouth feels dry
options.B: Reduce the dose slowly as advised by your doctor
options.C: Crush all the tablets so they clear your system faster
options.D: Double the dose if your tremors start coming back

explanation: You've got it! Stopping these meds suddenly can cause rebound muscle stiffness and make tremors flare up fiercely. Always taper safely!

question: What is the core focus of transactional leadership?

options.A: Giving staff complete independence
options.B: Inspiring a grand shared vision
options.C: Voting on every policy change
options.D: Rewards and punishments for performance

explanation: Transactional leaders use a system of rewards for meeting goals and corrections or punishments for failing to meet them. [learn more](GST321_U3_T3#GST321_U3_T3_h5)

question: Why are small, frequent meals often recommended for patients with poor appetites?

options.A: They prevent the patient from feeling overwhelmed by large food portions.
options.B: They guarantee that the patient will eat the exact same calories.
options.C: They cure chronic digestive disorders within twenty-four hours.
options.D: They stop the kitchen staff from having to cook three times a day.

explanation: Large meal trays often discourage weak or nauseated patients, whereas smaller portions look manageable and encourage better overall intake. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T023#GNS227_U2_T023_h8)

question: On an ECG machine, what does the QRS complex show us?

options.A: The heart resting and recovering
options.B: Upper chambers squeezing
options.C: Lower chambers relaxing
options.D: Lower chambers electrical activity before they squeeze

explanation: The big tall spike on the ECG screen (the QRS) is the electrical wave racing through the ventricles right before they pump blood out.

question: What does an "unmet need" for family planning mean?

options.A: Using birth control despite wanting to get pregnant
options.B: Being unable to find a pediatrician in a rural clinic
options.C: Experiencing side effects from modern oral pills
options.D: Wanting to avoid pregnancy but using no contraception

explanation: An 'unmet need' describes women who are ready and wanting to delay or stop having children, but aren't currently using any form of birth control.

question: Why doesn't it work to treat only the female patient while completely ignoring her sexual partners?

options.A: It frequently leads to immediate reinfection of the patient
options.B: It stops the patient's immune system from producing antibodies
options.C: It causes the laboratory tests to show false positive results
options.D: It automatically makes the bacteria resistant to all antibiotics

explanation: It's a cycle! If the partner still has the infection, sleeping together again will just pass it right back to her.

question: Why must mast cell stabilizer sprays or drops be used regularly *before* an allergy season starts?

options.A: They interact with stomach acid if taken after an allergic attack starts.
options.B: They prevent cell rupture proactively but cannot reverse a reaction already underway.
options.C: They build up a thick physical barrier inside the nose that blocks dust.
options.D: They take at least two full weeks to enter the bloodstream for the first time.

explanation: Exactly! Think of them as prevention champs—they stop cells from popping, but they can't clean up the mess if the histamine has already spilled out.

question: Where should used hypodermic needles and scalpel blades be disposed of immediately after use?

options.A: Black domestic waste bins
options.B: Puncture-resistant safety boxes
options.C: Cardboard packaging boxes
options.D: Open plastic wash basins

explanation: Sharps must always go into dedicated, puncture-proof safety containers to prevent accidental needle-stick injuries. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T6#GNS122_U2_T6_h8)

question: How do researchers ethically manage control groups when testing a new treatment?

options.A: By making sure the control group pays for their own hospital stay
options.B: By hiding the true purpose of the study from the hospital staff
options.C: By refusing to give any care at all to the control group
options.D: By giving the control group standard nursing care instead of nothing

explanation: Providing standard care ensures patients in the control group are not neglected or harmed while still allowing comparison against the new intervention. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T7#GNS224_U1_T7_h7)

question: Children playing barefoot in dirt can catch hookworm. What is actually happening in the soil?

options.A: The shed ova are maturing into infectious forms in the earth.
options.B: The soil is actively generating new adult worms without eggs.
options.C: The eggs are dissolving completely into harmless minerals.
options.D: The dirt is killing all parasites with natural plant toxins.

explanation: Warm, moist soil gives many parasite eggs the incubator time they need to become infectious to humans. Exactly right!

question: How do money worries directly affect a patient who has been given a referral?

options.A: Patients may refuse or delay going because they cannot afford hospital fees
options.B: Hospitals automatically waive all bills for referred community patients
options.C: The government refunds transport money upon arrival at the gate
options.D: Patients receive double the amount of free drugs to compensate

explanation: So true. Because many people pay out-of-pocket, financial hardship often forces vulnerable patients to stay home instead of getting the specialist care they need.

question: Which important hormone does the placenta make to keep early pregnancy going strong?

options.A: Follicle-stimulating hormone
options.B: Human chorionic gonadotropin
options.C: Prolactin
options.D: Oxytocin

explanation: This is the famous hormone (hCG) detected by pregnancy tests! It signals the body to protect the pregnancy during those crucial first few weeks.

question: You are teaching a client with heart failure how to avoid fluid buildup at home. What is the best advice to give?

options.A: Go to the emergency room every time you feel slightly tired
options.B: Stop taking your water pills whenever you feel thirsty
options.C: Drink extra water throughout the day to flush out toxins
options.D: Weigh yourself every morning at the same time and report sudden gains

explanation: You nailed it! Daily morning weights are a quick and reliable way to spot early fluid retention before it becomes dangerous.

question: Which clinical sign is most characteristic of kwashiorkor?

options.A: Severe muscle wasting with no body fat at all
options.B: Rapid overgrowth of the long bones
options.C: Generalized pitting edema and skin changes
options.D: An extremely high fever with sudden seizures

explanation: Kwashiorkor happens when a child lacks enough protein. A classic giveaway is swelling (edema) in the body and noticeable skin changes.

question: What is the primary goal of medical detoxification in substance abuse care?

options.A: To isolate the patient from all family members during therapy
options.B: To teach the patient new vocational skills for finding employment
options.C: To permanently cure the psychological desire to use drugs again
options.D: To safely clear the substance from the body while managing withdrawal symptoms

explanation: Spot on! Detox is all about physical stabilization—getting the drug out of the system safely while doctors and nurses help manage the rough withdrawal symptoms.
